doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Whether improvisers think while playing
summary: Both say they think about chords; Aebersold rarely plays without conscious thought.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I wish I had a — let’s see — thirty dollars for every time I’ve asked the question to jazz musicians, what are you thinking about when you play, and the answer is, “I’m not.”

I think too. Maybe their definition of thinking is different from mine but I still am at the point where if I’m playing a standard, improvising on a standard, I’m thinking about the chords as they’re going by.

Yeah. I am too. I’ve had a few instances, not very many, where I actually play something and it might be like a major or six beats or possibly two measures long where I’m not consciously thinking. And when that passes and I’m still playing, I’m thinking back on that. Boy that was neat. And I think at times I also think is that what these people are saying when they’re not thinking? You know. But it’s just automatic? If that’s the case © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
then I’ve still got a whole lot of playing to do to get to the stage where I consistently play without thinking.
